text:
Predicates:
Wins(x, y) ::: x wins against y.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
InMovie(x) ::: x is in the movie.
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are the good guys.
BadGuys(x) ::: x are the bad guys.
HeroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is the nemesis of y.
Year(x, y) ::: x is the year y.

Premises:
∀x (HeroMovie(x) → ∃y (NamedAfter(x, y) ∧ GoodGuys(y))) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
HeroMovie(surprisingAdventures) ∧ NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
Fights(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ∀y ((Fights(x, y) ∧ Wins(x, y)) → ¬Wins(y, x)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting does not win.
∀x (NamedAfter(x, y) → InMovie(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is in the movie.

Conclusion:
¬Wins(nemesis, sirDigby) ::: Sir Digby's nemesis does not win.
